notes: v466 — "why is PROMISING always zero?" Because the three tiles count SHARES, but a tier belongs to a SIGNAL — and the two are linked by the very thing the tier measures. A signal earns SOLID by firing hundreds of times, and firing hundreds of times is exactly what makes it tag hundreds of shares. A signal is TOO EARLY because it has barely fired — so it tags almost nobody. The share-tiles lean to SOLID by construction, not by luck. The distribution you were actually looking for is now printed underneath: "19 signals: 12 proven · 1 promising · 6 unproven" — and THAT one is bottom-heavy, because several signals haven't fired once all year. Lesson 46 explains it properly. Hard-refresh (Ctrl+F5) to update.
